review: 2:1–2:2 צֶלֶם אֱלֹהִים … וּבוֹ כֹל נִבְרָא — Colossians 1:15–16 (צֶלֶם הָאֱלֹהִים … כָּל־דָּבָר נִבְרָא בוֹ); the Arabic صُورَةُ اللهِ بِهِ / وَلَهُ الْكُلُّ خُلِق is that passage.
2:3–2:4 הוּא בְּכוֹר … הַכֹּל גַּם־נִפְדָּה — the Arabic splits الْـ / ـكُلُّ across the line break; Hebrew cannot split a word, so 'all' is repeated at the head of the second clause instead.
3:3 הִשְׁלִים אוֹתָנוּ — 'He reconciled us' (Col 1:20, הַשְׁלִים); the Arabic صَالَحَنَا is the same verb, and the hiph'il of שלם is its fixed Hebrew rendering.
4:3 אֵין בָּנוּ חֶסֶר — 'there is no lack in us'; the Arabic مَا بِنَا نَقْصٌ is the same negation, and חֶסֶר is the biblical noun for what is lacking (Eccl 1:15).
5:1 שַׁיָּכוּתֵנוּ — 'our belonging', for انْتِسَابُنَا; the noun is post-biblical, but the abstract is required and the biblical alternative (לְךָ אֲנַחְנוּ) would need a whole clause.
